cards.text: Ezekiel, a prophet living among the exiles in Babylon, tells this one himself (Ezekiel 1:1-3). Back at the start, God had him act out Jerusalem under siege as a sign to Israel (Ezekiel 4:1-3). Now, in the twelfth year of exile, on the fifth day of the tenth month, a man who escaped from Jerusalem finds him.

cards.question: What news does the man who escaped from Jerusalem bring Ezekiel?

cards.text: Here's the timing. The evening before the man arrives, the hand of the LORD is on Ezekiel.

cards.question: Before the man who escaped from Jerusalem shows up in the morning, the LORD opens Ezekiel's ___.

cards.text: Ezekiel is no longer mute. Mouth open, back in business! Then the word of the LORD comes: the people living in the ruins back in Israel are saying that Abraham, Israel's forefather, was only one man, yet he possessed the land.

cards.question: Abraham was only one man, yet he possessed the land. So why do the people in the ruins think the land surely belongs to them?

answers.text: Because there are many of them

cards.text: Hey, I'd try that math too: ONE coworker gets a raise, there's FIFTY of us in the break room, so surely we're ALL getting one! But God tells Ezekiel what to say back to them.

cards.question: God tells Ezekiel to say that the people in the ruins eat meat with the blood in it, look to their idols and shed blood. What does God then ask them?

answers.text: Whether they should possess the land
Whether they will rebuild the walls

cards.text: God's list keeps going: they've relied on their swords, committed detestable acts, and each one has defiled his neighbor's wife. Then that question again: should they possess the land?
Then God says, "As surely as I live…" and lays it out. The ones in the ruins will fall by the sword, and the ones in the open field He will give to wild animals to be devoured.

cards.question: God says those in the ruins will fall by the sword, and those in the open field will go to wild animals. What does He say about the ones in the strongholds and caves?

cards.text: God says He will make the land a desolate waste, and the pride of her strength will come to an end. This part is heavy, friend.

cards.question: God says the mountains of Israel will become so desolate that no one will pass through.
God says He will make the land a desolate waste even though the people have done nothing wrong.
God says He'll make the land a desolate waste because of all the abominations the people have committed. When He does, what does He say they will know?

cards.text: Then God tells Ezekiel that his people are talking about him near the city walls and in the doorways of their houses. They're passing the word along, one to another.

cards.question: The people near the walls and doorways pass the word about Ezekiel to each other. What do they say?

answers.text: Come and hear the message from the LORD
Stay far away from that prophet
That prophet has lost his mind

cards.text: Ezekiel is the hottest ticket in town, and in all my junk drawer years NOBODY ever told a friend to come hear the stamper! So his people come as usual and sit before him to hear his words.

cards.question: Ezekiel's crowd hears his words, but hearing is only half of it. What does God say they don't do?
God says the hearts of Ezekiel's crowd match the love they express with their mouths.

cards.text: God says their hearts pursue dishonest gain. Then He tells Ezekiel what he's like to them.

cards.question: To the people who come and hear him, what does God say Ezekiel is like?

cards.text: A singer with a beautiful voice, who skillfully plays an instrument! It's like your boss gives the whole team a serious warning, and everybody claps, says "GREAT meeting!" and changes NOTHING.

cards.question: When Ezekiel's message comes to pass, God says the people will know that a ___ has been among them.
